A B S T R A C T
Low-density steels have garnered significant attention due to the demand for lightweight structural materials in
aerospace and automobile industries. However, manufacturing low-density steels with different hardness levels
poses challenges in composition design, processing optimization, and the application of hardening techniques
across various alloy systems. In this work, Fe-35Mn-(15, 17, 19)Al-5Cu (at.%) low-density steels with an ultra-
wide flexible hardness ranging from 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV through simple aging treatments were developed,
attributing to the continuous precipitation of the ultra-hard β-Mn phase. The densities of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu steels
were regulated by varying the Al contents, and the effects of Al contents on the aging hardening behaviors of Fe-
Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels were systematically investigated. The results show that the increase of Al content led
to the decrease in precipitation kinetics of β-Mn. Moreover, increasing Al content slightly enhanced the intrinsic
hardness of β-Mn. However. it also led to the decrease of FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces and the
decrease in the fracture toughness of the ultra-hard alloys. This resulted in the decrease in the final hardening
effect of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels with increasing Al content. Due to the advantages of ultra-high hardness
(965.6 HV) and low density, our Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu low-density steel achieved an ultra-high specific
hardness of 141 HV⋅cm<sup>3</sup>/g.

3.2. Evolutions of constituent phases after different aging treatments

(Body-centered cubic, BCC) phase formed in the solution-treated Fe-Mn-
Al-Cu low-density steels. To clarify the microstructural origin of the
rapid aging hardening behaviors of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels,
EBSD characterization was performed on these alloys subjected to
different aging treatments. Fig. 4 presents the EBSD results of the 15Al
alloy after different aging treatments. After aging at 525 <sup>◦</sup>C for 3 h, it is
evident that a significant amount of β-Mn had precipitated (85.8 %),
with only a small amount of α matrix remaining untransformed. The

solid-solution state to 872.0 HV, indicating the strong hardening effect
of the β-Mn phase. After aging at
5 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }
for 6 h, the α matrix had almost
entirely transformed into β-Mn. Furthermore, a new fine BCC phase was
present within the β-Mn. Following aging at 650 <sup>◦</sup>C for 3 h, the un
transformed α regions were no longer observed, and a new FCC phase
was distributed in β-Mn.

5. Conclusions
In this work, we systematically investigated the effects of Al contents
on the aging hardening behaviors of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels
subjected to different aging treatments and derived the following
conclusions:
1) An ultra-wide flexible hardness ranging from 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV
was tailored in Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels with different Al
contents. Due to the combination of ultra-high hardness and low-
density advantages, the Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu alloy achieved an
ultrahigh specific hardness of 141 HV⋅cm<sup>3</sup>/g.
2) The increase in Al contents slowed down the precipitation kinetics of
β-Mn during aging treatments, which led to the complete trans
formation from α to β-Mn being extended.
3) The increase in Al content slightly enhanced the intrinsic hardness of
β-Mn. However, it also led to the decrease of FCC Cu-rich phase
between β-Mn interfaces and the decrease in the fracture toughness
of the ultra-hard alloys. This resulted in the decrease in the final
hardening effect of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels with increasing
Al content.

5. Conclusions
In this work, we systematically investigated the effects of Al contents
on the aging hardening behaviors of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels
subjected to different aging treatments and derived the following
conclusions:
1) An ultra-wide flexible hardness ranging from 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV
was tailored in Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels with different Al
contents. Due to the combination of ultra-high hardness and low-
density advantages, the Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu alloy achieved an
ultrahigh specific hardness of 141 HV⋅cm<sup>3</sup>/g.
2) The increase in Al contents slowed down the precipitation kinetics of
β-Mn during aging treatments, which led to the complete trans
formation from α to β-Mn being extended.
3) The increase in Al content slightly enhanced the intrinsic hardness of
β-Mn. However, it also led to the decrease of FCC Cu-rich phase
between β-Mn interfaces and the decrease in the fracture toughness
of the ultra-hard alloys. This resulted in the decrease in the final
hardening effect of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels with increasing
Al content.
